svg.title: SG.2 — Layered city theme composition board
svg.desc: Draft combined behavior and artwork board showing one theme across morning, noon, dusk, and night; theme layers, auxiliary details, time-linked ambient element, fallback, compact, and reduced-motion behavior.
svg.text: OXYGEN · SCENE GENERATION · SG.2
Board 1 of 2 · City behavior and composition
One city composition; time-of-day treatment, forecast layers, and ambient details resolve together at the selected instant.
SCHEMATIC · APPROVED
SAME THEME · FOUR SELECTED-TIME STATES
TIME LINK
Ambient marker follows selected local time along a theme-designed path; scene does not run on an independent clock.
Illustrative path only · no solar position, sunrise, sunset, or moon-phase claim
COMPOSITION CONTRACT · SEMANTIC GROUPS CAN OCCUPY DIFFERENT DEPTHS
BACK TO FRONT · CITY EXAMPLE
AUXILIARY · NON-WEATHER DETAIL
A semantic group, placed at theme-chosen depths

g.text: off by day · on at night
Street lights and small city details
Birds or other optional scene accents

svg.text: Auxiliary elements can sit behind, between, or in front of weather art.
They never change or imply forecast facts.
Other themes may reorder, combine, or omit these roles; no universal sky / ground / horizon is required.
BEHAVIOR, FALLBACK & QUALITY
PORTRAIT
COMPACT
Scene stays above tape.
Keep time legible;
reduce optional detail.
STATIC / REDUCED MOTION
Element stays at selected-time position.
Missing optional auxiliary variant → omit the detail.
Missing phase backdrop → reuse base city + phase palette.
Never replace a forecast meaning with decorative fallback.
Use reusable static shapes, simple palette / visibility changes; no continuous 3D scene.
BOARD INTENT & REVIEW BOUNDARY
This board defines one theme’s behavior, layer placement, time-linked variants, auxiliary semantics, and fallback.
It does not add providers, weather facts, theme selection, downloads, or exact astronomical behavior.
SG.2 proposes composition only. SG.3 owns clear / cloudy / light rendering; later slices own precipitation and other event families.
BOARD 1 OF 2 · APPROVED 2026-10-31
